div.p: This paper presents a mathematical model to determine the optimal length of static messages that can achieve more efficient use of a FlexRay network. In order to determine the optimal length of static message, the proposed model evaluates the given set of messages with respect to a network utilization index, which is defined in this work. The efficient use of a FlexRay network is achieved by reallocating any static message whose length is equal or greater than the resulting value to the dynamic segment. The effectiveness of the proposed method is investigated by applying to the SAE benchmark data.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: A networked control system can be defined as a control system wherein the control loops are closed through a real-time network [1]. Networked control systems offer various advantages over traditional centralized control in terms of the flexibility, efficiency, maintenance and installation costs, reliability and safety, etc. All of these advantages have made networked control be considered in a wide range of industry, including safety-critical applications such as aerospace and "xby-wire" cars. "X-by-wire" is a network-based vehicle control system in which hydraulics and mechanical linkages are replaced by fieldbuses and smart devices. Since safety-critical applications like "x-by-wire" require extreme requirements on the reliability and safety to be met, it is essential to develop a highly reliable communication network protocol. Most of transmission messages are real-time message; their transmission time must be guaranteed.

One of the first in-vehicle communication networks for automotive system is the controller area network (CAN) [3], [13]. However, it is not suitable for safety-critical applications like "X-by-wire" car. Because CAN protocol cannot satisfies requirement of application such as hard real time, high-speed, robust, and predictable communication. To resolve these issues, FlexRay [10] is a de facto standard in-vehicle developed by automotive industry for the purpose of applying to safetycritical systems.

A FlexRay message consists of two segments, the static segment and the dynamic segment, in order to support both event-triggered and time-triggered protocols. Event-triggered protocols generate message by event occurrence and have to be transmitted in deadline. This protocol has many advantages in terms of high flexibility, extendibility and efficiency at a low bus load. In contrast, time-triggered protocols exhibit a deterministic temporal behavior which is crucial for hard realtime systems [2]. The static segment of FlexRay operates on the basis of time-division multiple accesses (TDMA) which is a time-triggered protocol, while the dynamic segment operates based on Flexible TDMA (FTDMA) to implement an eventtriggered protocol [11]. It is straightforward that the static segment is used to transmit hard real-time periodic messages, while the dynamic segment is used to transmit sporadic messages [2], [3]. Therefore, in order to achieve an efficient use of the FlexRay network, it is essential to apply a proper scheduling algorithm for the both segments.

Previous work on the static segment has focused on the timing analysis [4], or on heuristic strategies [5]. Schmidt et al. investigated the message frame packing that maximizes network efficiency by reducing unused slots [6], [7]. They packed the signals into same size messages to obey the restrictions of the FlexRay protocol, while using little bandwidth. And then formulate a nonlinear integer programming problem to maximize bandwidth utilization. They also proposed a scheduling method with low jitter and minimum number of frame identifies (FIDs) to improve the network efficiency. However, these methods show a drawback of using only part of static slots. Recently, Kang et al. have proposed a scheduling algorithm to reduce the network utilization by reallocating static messages with the longest length to the dynamic segment [8]. It is using characteristic of FlexRay protocol that length of static slot is determined by the longest static message. Therefore by reallocating the longest static message into the dynamic segment, length of static slot is reduced and network efficiency is improved. However, the use of the longest message as a guideline for reallocations does not guarantee the minimum network utilization due to the number and the length of static messages. This paper proposes a scheduling algorithm for static messages that can minimize the FlexRay network utilization. The proposed method is based on the optimal length of static message which is determined by evaluating the given set of messages in the network with respect to a network utilization index. By reallocating any static messages whose length are equal or greater than the resulting optimal length to the dynamic segment, more efficient use of a FlexRay network can be achieved. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated by applying to the SAE benchmark data [9].

In the next section, section II presents the architecture of FlexRay protocol and application system model. The system model is defined, and formula that finds an optimal size of static message to minimize network utilization is introduced. Section III describes a proposed scheduling algorithm and result of FlexRay static message scheduling using proposed algorithm in detail. Conclusions are given in Section IV.

div.head: II. SYSTEM MODEL
div.p: The FlexRay communication system consist nodes that connected by one FlexRay communication channel (see Figure 1. Each processing node connected to a FlexRay bus is composed of two main components: a Host CPU, Communication Controller (CC) and Controller-Host Interface (CHI). The controller runs independently of the node's CPU and implements the FlexRay protocol services.

In this work, it is assumed that the FlexRay network communicates under the following assumptions: z There are no transmission error and failure in the communication system; and, z All of the messages to be sent through the FlexRay network are known, including priority, message type, deadline, and message period.

div.head: C. Static Message Scheduling Algorithm
div.p: Static message scheduling algorithm is implemented to minimize network utilization under following conditions.
All FlexRay messages should be scheduled within worst case response time. That means schedulability constraint should be satisfied.

The static message scheduling algorithm is executed for reducing network utilization. There are initial network parameter values and the proposed scheduling algorithm for static messages is executed repeatedly in the following steps:
Find an optimal length of static messages that minimizes the network utilization index of (1); 2)
Reallocate the resulting static messages to the dynamic segment; 3)
Calculate the schedulability constraint [12] and the network utilization; and, 4)
Repeat steps 1) -3) until both the schedulability constraint and the minimum network utilization are satisfied.

This scheduling is finished when there is no more message to reallocate to the dynamic segment. If there is not satisfied the schedulability constraint that means schedulability is 0, another optimal message is searched. If the schedulability is 1 and the network utilization is reduced, the optimal static message is reallocate to the dynamic segment. Schedulability is calculated by cumulative multiplication of each message's schedulability. Schedulability of each message is 1 means that worst case response time is less than transmission deadline, otherwise it is 0. In other word, the system is schedulable means that worst case response times of all messages are in deadline. To find optimal static message, we assumed there are m messages in the order of size. div.head: III. SIMULATION RESULTS
div.p: The SAE benchmark data and frame packing table [8] are used in order to compare the previous work with the proposed scheduling algorithm in this paper. The SAE benchmark report describes a set of signals sent between seven different subsystems in a prototype electric car. SAE benchmark data has 53 signals used for class C application. The signals have information about data size, transmission period, type of signal, deadline and transmission node.

To transmit each SAE benchmark signal, using FlexRay message frame independently is inefficient. As known in FlexRay message frame format, it has 8 bytes overhead (head segment and trailer segment) and is required additional bits for transmitting physical layers. If using dynamic segment, the Dynamic Trailing Sequence is also needed. Therefore it need message frame packing firstly to improve efficiency more than using original message frame. The signals that have same transmission node and period should be packed into same frame.

div.head: IV. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, a mathematical model to determine the static message length minimizing the FlexRay network utilization has been presented. The optimal length of static message can be calculated by evaluating the given set of messages with respect to a network utilization index, which is defined in this work. A more efficient use of the FlexRay network can be achieved by reallocating any static messages whose length is equal or greater than the resulting optimal length into the dynamic segment. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been demonstrated by applying to the SAE benchmark data. For further work, it is necessary to develop a scheduling algorithm considering both the static segment and the dynamic segment.
